messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: P2 - increased 4xx/timeout rate for embeddings endpoint /v1/embeddings (dedicated + hosted, ap-southeast-1). Triggered 2026-04-12T17:12:02Z. Pager: https://pager.redwood.example/inc/8123

oncall-bot: Summary: sudden rise in client 429s and some streaming timeouts. Suspected cause: tokenization errors or a throttling regression. Suggested runbook: https://playbooks.redwood.internal/oncall/embeddings-4xx

tara_p: taking this as primary. pulling recent deploys and quota configs.

beno: i'm secondary. if it's quota-related i can check rate-limit service and policy push history.

mike_z: quick glance at rpms and quota-meter: we see a spike in short-burst requests from a single API key cluster at 17:11:30 UTC, followed by 429s when the burst exceeded burst-window. Not seeing worker OOMs.

rachel: any recent deploys to embeddings-service? I saw a canary earlier today that changed token-bucket implementation.

mike_z: yes canary id: embeddings-ci/2026-04-12_1609 toggled new token-bucket refactor. Diff snippet:
```
- token_bucket: rate=100rps, burst=1000
+ token_bucket: rate=100rps, burst=200
```
Looks like burst was reduced to 200 in that canary and accidentally rolled to prod.

beno: if burst dropped from 1000->200 that would explain the 429s for batched embedding requests. rolling back should be first step.

tara_p: rolling token-bucket param back to burst=1000 for ap-southeast-1 via config service: `curl -X POST https://config.redwood.internal/kv -d '{"key":"embeddings/burst/ap-southeast-1","value":1000}'`

infra-bot: config rollback executed by tara_p. New value: burst=1000. Propagation to edge ~30s.

mike_z: propagation verified, 429 rate dropping. tail latency improving.

rachel: nice catch. can we also add a short-term mitigation to apply request-size limiting for single-request batch sizes > 512 to avoid hammering?

tara_p: putting an edge rule to limit batch-size to 512 for 20 minutes: `POST /api/internal/edge-rule -d '{"max_batch":512,"duration_m":20}'`

beno: filing followups: INF-3410 (root cause: token-bucket regression from canary -> prod), INF-3411 (add pre-deploy config diff check), INF-3412 (add batch-size alert). links: https://tickets.redwood.example/INF-3410 , https://tickets.redwood.example/INF-3411 , https://tickets.redwood.example/INF-3412

mike_z: customer impact: about 0.4% of embedding requests in ap-southeast-1 received 429s between 17:11:20 and 17:18:00 UTC. Two Dedicated customers saw transient rate limiting but no SLA violations flagged yet. Support pinged.

rachel: handoff in 18 minutes -> tara to beno. Tara please leave explicit notes for handoff and any remaining mitigations.

tara_p: Handoff notes -> primary -> beno at 17:30 UTC:
- status: rollback applied, edge batch-size rule applied, metrics trending down. Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring.
- mitigations: config rollback to burst=1000, edge batch-size limit 512 (20m).
- tickets: INF-3410 (assigned rachel) for RCA + canary gating change, INF-3411 (assigned eng-ci) for deploy diff check, INF-3412 (assigned observability) for batch alert.
- runbook: https://playbooks.redwood.internal/oncall/embeddings-4xx (steps: confirm quota settings, rollback param, apply edge protections, notify customers)
- helpers: `kubectl get pods -l app=embeddings -n prod | grep ap-southeast-1`, `kubectl logs <pod> -c embeddings --since=15m`, `curl https://metrics.redwood.internal/query?m=embeddings.4xx.rate&region=ap-southeast-1`

beno: i'll take primary at 17:30 UTC. i'll keep the batch-size rule in place until 17:50 or until 4xx drops below 0.5% for 10m.

infra-bot: handoff recorded. primary: beno, secondary: mike_z.

rachel: scheduling retro: Wed 2026-04-14 09:00 UTC. Zoom: https://zoom.redwood/meet/infra-retro-8123. Invite created and linked to INF-3410.

beno: quick action items list:
- rachel / INF-3410: write RCA, include canary->prod rollout timeline and propose gating rule for config changes.
- eng-ci / INF-3411: add a validation that flags large burst reductions (>50%) in config diffs.
- observability / INF-3412: create alert on sudden drop in token-bucket burst and on batch-size spikes.
- support: confirm the two Dedicated customers have no outstanding cases, offer follow-up if needed.

mike_z: leaving additional logs in INF-3410 (routing + token-bucket metrics).

tara_p: thanks team. handing over primary to beno now. :thumbsup:

beno: taking primary. i'll escalate to oncall lead if 4xx > 1% for 5m. keeping monitoring for 40m then sign off.

oncall-bot: incident update: state=monitoring, last_message_ts marker."
